chapter: Benny Carter, saxophones and Coleman Hawkins's last years
title: Teaching jazz at City College, and Paul Quinichette as a Lester Young copy
summary: Caldwell tells students to find their own sound; Quinichette copies Lester Young well yet keeps some independence, like Ben Webster.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Yeah, because you got these classes. Like I did a jazz seminar over there where I worked, for City College, and I got to do one probably the end of the month. But I never would go into the full detail of theory and harmony and composition, like that, just on the chord basis and that when these fellows wonder, how did you do this with the chords. You can invert the chord, whatever you want to feel like, I said, because you got to hear it first, and then you use your own ideas. It's good to copy after

somebody else, I said, but it's best to try to get your own that can distinguish you from the other people, you know. I said, you can steal, I said, but you become prolific with it, if you do, then you're not doing nothing but like copy after Lester. Like this boy, Paul Quinichette Protege.
Well, he's a good copy.
Good copy, see. And they call him Vice Pres.
Right.
(Unintelligible).
He really is the best copy I—
Yes, he was. He's still playing. He's here in New York.
He's got a -- I mean he really got it down.

Yes, he has. He has. I saw him. We were supposed to be together at the Jazz Museum with Jack Bradley Bryant, but I couldn't make it because I just got out of the hospital. I had this thing (Unintelligible) at the Biltmore Hotel three days later, and it just mean I couldn't make both of them, because that was more for me, that Biltmore Hotel, because Jack called me up and sent (unintelligible) for me. But he may change a little bit too.
Who, Paul?
Yes, he has. He didn't -- you know,
before he went -- left New York. I don't know. Maybe he went out West somewheres, about --
Well, he was -- oh, he really was at one point quite poor. He was practically a bum.
Yes, I heard that.

Then he started working in radio repairs or something. I don't think, (unintelligible) well he may have done. But, no, he -- I mean that's a strange thing that he does. He's a copy, and yet he has a certain -- he has a certain independence of Lester.
Yes, he has.
You know, it's like when we first began to hear Ben Webster. He said that was a copy of Hall. Do you remember that?
That's right.
But, you know, you wouldn't take him seriously at first (unintelligible).
